market_specific_notes: USCIS operates a blanket designation: “We recognize all state and local health departments as civil surgeons, and they are authorized to complete the vaccination assessments for refugees seeking adjustment of status.” For Seattle that names Public Health – Seattle & King County. It covers the vaccination assessment for refugees adjusting status, not the full examination for everyone.

USCIS also designates military physicians as civil surgeons at military treatment facilities in the United States, for US veterans, members of the US military and designated dependents. If that describes you, the route is different from the one the locator shows.
Everyone else uses a designated civil surgeon found through the federal locator. Confirming which of the three routes applies to you saves more time than comparing prices does.

Before you use the checklist below, settle which of the three routes applies to you — refugee adjusting status, military or veteran, or neither. The rest of the comparison only makes sense once that is decided.
local_vetting_points: Search uscis.gov/tools/find-a-civil-surgeon by your ZIP rather than by city name — a Seattle search and a 98xxx search do not return the same list.
Confirm the office's designation in that federal tool, not in a directory or a review site.
Ask whether the practice completes the tuberculosis testing on site.
Ask what happens if a vaccination record cannot be located.
Confirm whether the price quoted assumes you arrive with complete records.
typical_cost_ranges: No authority publishes a price for this examination. USCIS: “Fees for immigration medical examinations are established by the civil surgeon. Fees may vary by civil surgeon.”
USCIS advises calling several offices, and says the cost “can vary significantly”. Treat that as an instruction rather than a disclaimer.
Get each quote itemised: examination, tuberculosis and syphilis testing, missing vaccines, completing and sealing the form, and any second visit.
There is no USCIS filing fee for Form I-693 — it is $0. The published money is the underlying application: I-485 paper $1,440 or online $1,390 for an applicant over 14.
payment_options: USCIS tells applicants to confirm acceptable forms of payment with the civil surgeon's office beforehand.
Bring the insurance card, and ask the specific question: does this practice accept this plan for immigration medical examinations? USCIS warns many plans do not cover all portions of the exam.
wait_time_notes: The waiting that matters is not the appointment queue but the gap between the visit and the signed form. Ask about the second one.
Sent-out laboratory work and a chest X-ray after a positive tuberculosis test are the two most common reasons a one-visit plan becomes a three-week one.
availability_notes: Ask whether same-week availability refers to the examination alone or to a completed form.
If you have a filing deadline, name the date on the call and ask the office to commit or decline.
named_resources_or_providers: USCIS Find a Civil Surgeon locator (official) — uscis.gov/tools/find-a-civil-surgeon
Public Health – Seattle & King County — kingcounty.gov/en/dept/dph. USCIS recognises local health departments as civil surgeons for the refugee vaccination assessment.
USCIS Form I-693 page — uscis.gov/i-693, for the current form edition and filing instructions.
Listings are neutral examples and starting points for your own verification. Nothing here is a ranking or an endorsement.
city_intro_override: Seattle sits inside King County, and the county's public health service is the one named body in this process that USCIS itself recognises. Knowing which route applies to you — a private civil surgeon or a health department — is the first decision, and it depends on your immigration category, not your postcode.

primary_city_decision_block.title: Local civil surgeon comparison checklist
items: Establish first whether you are a refugee adjusting status, military or veteran, or neither — the routes differ.
If neither: search uscis.gov/tools/find-a-civil-surgeon by ZIP and verify designation there.
Ask for an itemised price covering examination, labs, vaccines, form completion and follow-up.
Collect the vaccination records USCIS names before the first visit.
Tell the office whether the I-485 goes by mail or online, so the envelope is handled correctly.
Confirm the form edition and the date the civil surgeon intends to sign.

heading: Seattle and King County: which civil surgeon route applies to you
i693_document_requirements: Form I-693 in the edition USCIS currently accepts.

Government-issued photo identification such as a valid passport or driver's licence; for applicants aged 14 or younger, identification showing name, date and place of birth and a parent's full name, such as a birth certificate with an English translation, or an affidavit.

Your vaccination or immunisation record. The list USCIS names is DT, DTP, DTaP, Td, Tdap, OPV, IPV, MMR, Hib, Hepatitis A, Hepatitis B, Varicella, Pneumococcal, Influenza, Rotavirus and Meningococcal disease.
Payment, in a form the office has confirmed it takes.
vaccination_handling_notes: Missing records are the most expensive thing you can bring to this appointment, because the alternatives are repeat doses or serology.
Washington maintains a statewide immunisation information system through which residents can request their own record; ask the clinic what record format it accepts before you order anything.
Refugees adjusting status may have the vaccination assessment completed at a state or local health department under the blanket designation described above.
bilingual_support: The USCIS locator lets you filter by Languages Spoken from a long list of named languages, and by doctor's sex. Both are declarations the practice made to USCIS.
Filtering tells you a language is available in the practice. Ask separately whether it is available during the form review, which is the part that matters.
appointment_booking_notes: Before the exam, decide how the I-485 is being filed. By mail: the envelope stays sealed. Online: USCIS instructs you to open it and upload the form, then keep the original and the envelope until the case is decided.
Ask the office which edition of the form it completes. For signatures dated 3 July 2025 or later, USCIS accepts only the 01/20/25 edition.
Ask whether the appointment covers intake, examination and paperwork or only the first of the three.

Ask how the sealed packet is released — collected in person, or posted — and what the correction process is if an error is found after you have it. Offices differ sharply on the second, and it only matters once it matters.
